summary:
PULSAR is an offline-capable, mobile-first health guide for astronauts who are not medical experts. It is a guide, not a diagnostic tool. Users create a simple profile and choose one of three modes: Space (the main mode), Field, or Home. Each mode has its own design and parameter set.

PULSAR covers temperature, blood pressure, heart rate, oxygen saturation, glucose, sleep, and mood. Every parameter has built-in help: what it is, how to use the measuring instrument step by step, and what the result means. Readings are color-coded with shape and text, and out-of-range values trigger alerts. Before measuring, the app checks for red-flag symptoms and runs a pre-measurement checklist that sets a reliability seal on the reading. Each result ends with what it means, what to do now, and when and to whom to escalate. In Space mode this accounts for communication delays.

It addresses the challenge by turning NASA’s documented hazards (isolation, closed environments, cardiovascular changes, hypoxia, nutrition) into simple, actionable guidance. Its Field and Home modes extend the same approach to geologists in remote terrain and to older adults with chronic conditions.

It matters because, on long missions, crews will need to act with delayed contact with Earth. Every range and text carries a source and an evidence-confidence level. Data stays on the device. Unfinished features are marked "🚧".
details:
What it does and how it works

PULSAR is a mobile-first health guide for people who are not medical experts, such as astronauts, field scientists and older adults. It is a guide, not a diagnostic tool. The user creates a simple profile (nickname, age, known conditions) and chooses one of three modes: Space (the main mode), Field or Home. Each mode has its own design and set of parameters.

For each parameter (temperature, blood pressure, heart rate, oxygen saturation, glucose, sleep and mood), the app provides:

  • Help in three parts: what the parameter is, how to use the measuring instrument step by step, and what the result means.
  • A red-flag symptom check before measuring. If a warning symptom is selected, the app skips the measurement and gives escalation advice.
  • A pre-measurement checklist that sets a reliability seal on the reading.
  • A result with a status (✓ Normal, ▲ Caution, ⚠ Alert), what it means, what to do now, and when and to whom to escalate. In Space mode the advice accounts for communication delay with Earth.

Status colors are always paired with a shape and a text label. Data is stored only on the user's device, and the app works offline. A history view shows trends. In this demo, history readings are simulated and labelled as such.

Benefits and intended impact

PULSAR turns the hazards NASA documents (isolation, closed environments, distance from Earth, altered gravity, radiation) into simple, actionable guidance. Its purpose is to help non-experts take measurements correctly, interpret them cautiously and know when to ask for help. The Field and Home modes extend the same approach to remote fieldwork and everyday care for people with chronic conditions.

Tools and technologies

  • App: single-file HTML, CSS and vanilla JavaScript, with SVG and canvas pixel art. It has no external dependencies apart from web fonts.
  • Storage: browser localStorage, with an in-memory fallback.
  • Testing: Playwright for automated click-through tests.
  • AI assistance: Claude (Anthropic) was used for development and for researching reference ranges.
  • Hardware: none. The app is designed to complement existing instruments (thermometer, blood pressure monitor, pulse oximeter, glucometer).

Creativity

The Space mode uses a retro synthwave pixel-art style with a procedurally drawn Saturn. The Field mode looks like a topographic field notebook, and the Home mode uses minimalist large type. The central idea is a guide that teaches proper instrument use and interpretation, not just a dashboard of numbers.

Factors we considered

  • Rigor: each range and help text carries a source and a confidence level (solid, weak evidence or draft), based on AHA/ACC, ADA, AASM/SRS and FDA guidance, plus NASA Human Research Program material. Content that contradicted the literature was removed from the manual we started from.
  • Safety: ranges are designed for adults, and the app shows a notice for minors and repeats the "repeat before acting" principle.
  • Accessibility: large touch targets, high contrast, and shape plus text alongside color.
  • Privacy: no servers and no data sharing.
  • Honesty about limits: unfinished features (wearable connection, radiation and vision modules, emergency contact, altitude correction, clinical validation) are visibly marked 🚧.
